sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Feisty Duck is an anchor for TLS, PKI and cryptography; we could link to it, wire it, check it, and graph its history.
sections.para: Run by Jelena and Ivan Ristić since 2009, Feisty Duck publishes Bulletproof TLS and PKI, a newsletter with over 50,000 subscribers, a free guide, a 174-event history and, since August, a news feed with LLM summaries. It shares our continuous publishing and curation. Integration ideas follow, but capturing its content needs permission under its terms and robots.txt.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: An expert anchor with news, newsletter, guide and history; integrate by linking and checking, copy only with permission.
sections.para: Feisty Duck curates SSL, TLS, PKI and cryptography with expertise and keeps it current. Its news monitors 37 sources with LLM summaries and hand-picked front pages. It has practised continuous publishing since 2009. We could anchor claims to it, build a crypto wire, add provenance and graph its history; a vault of its content needs permission.

sections.label: Brief: what Feisty Duck is
sections.line: A small London publisher since 2009, by the author of SSL Labs, built on continuous publishing.
sections.para: Feisty Duck focuses on security education, publishing Bulletproof TLS and PKI since 2014 and keeping it current, training more than 3,000 students since 2016, and starting Hardenize in 2018. Its content is written by someone who has spent many years on TLS and PKI, which makes it a source to trust.

sections.label: Feisty Duck News
sections.line: Feisty Duck News: 37 monitored sources, submissions, LLM summaries and a front page chosen by hand.
sections.para: Launched with newsletter issue #140 on 27 August 2026 to help curate the newsletter. Between 1 September and 25 October its feed held 100 items, led by post-quantum cryptography, PKI, cryptography and security. The 25 October front page covered Tor relays, Bitcoin, Edge CRL caching, OpenSSL 4.1.0 and Quad9; nothing on php2shell, which is not a cryptography story.

sections.label: The rest of the site
sections.line: The newsletter, a free guide updated in June, a 174-event history to 2029, and books with update dates.
sections.para: The monthly newsletter reaches over 50,000 subscribers, with recent issues on seven-day certificates and post-quantum cryptography. The Bulletproof TLS Guide is free online. The SSL/TLS and PKI History lists 174 dated, impact-scored events from SSL v2 in 1994 to 47-day certificates in 2029, nine dated 2026 or later.

sections.label: Debrief: what we share
sections.line: Continuous publishing, a curation pipeline, public source lists and history as data: much shared, with one caution.
sections.para: Feisty Duck's continuous books mirror versioned articles; its sources, submissions, LLM summaries and human promotion mirror the PHP site's collectors, curator and editor; its 37 public sources mirror the 913-page source watch. The same caution as Monstream applies: summaries are LLM-written, so readers need a quick, verified path from summary to unchanged original.

sections.label: How we could integrate
sections.line: Anchor crypto claims now; propose a crypto wire, verified summaries, a history graph, and testing for shorter certificates.
sections.para: Link sgit, passkey, signature and CSP claims to the guide, book and newsletter, as Wikipedia anchors php2shell. A fourth wire could follow Feisty Duck's public sources and credit its news. The researcher could capture, hash and check summaries of cited items. The 174 events could become a versioned graph. Shrinking certificate lifetimes test our own stack.

sections.label: Is there a need for a vault?
sections.line: A vault of our own links, notes and verdicts can be built now; captures of their pages need permission.
sections.para: The terms forbid reproducing or storing site content without separately agreed permission, and robots.txt disallows /news/ for all crawlers. So copying the news section or graphing the history waits for Feisty Duck's agreement, consistent with recording and respecting each source's licence and access.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Counts dated 25 October 2026; integrations proposed; nothing captured; the quality judgement is the editor's.
sections.para: The figures come from the public feed, source list and history data on 25 October 2026 and will change. No integration has been built and nothing was captured beyond reading the pages.
